clue.text: Protesting examinee could be so noticed

definitions.meaning: a candidate who disputes a grade asks for the exam paper to be assessed a second time
noticed in the sense of observed or commented upon

explanation.surface: An examinee who protests about a result gets attention for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first sense as RE-MARKED, hyphenated: marked again. The second sense is the ordinary word meaning observed or said.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is marked a second time, as a disputed script would be; the other is observed or commented, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Comes around again about nasty dogs

parts.note: re means about or concerning
curs are mongrels or nasty dogs

explanation.surface: Something keeps returning to the subject of vicious dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that recurs happens again, coming round once more.

clue.text: Evil male set in line

parts.note: to align is to set in a line

explanation.surface: A wicked man placed in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Malign as an adjective means harmful or wicked.

clue.text: Bought back foreign currency, some to be pocketed

indicators.note: the word some is put into the pocket made by the currency

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone repurchased foreign money and kept some for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketed' reads as stealing money; here it means placed inside, and 'foreign currency' is the South African rand.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransom a captive is to buy their release, redeeming them for payment.

clue.text: Garden weeded endlessly? Only some of it

indicators.note: only a part of the phrase weeded endlessly gives the letters

explanation.surface: A garden that is always being weeded, though only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in weedED ENdlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical paradise where Adam and Eve lived was a garden.

clue.text: Couples in British competitions

parts.note: races are competitions of speed

explanation.surface: Pairs taking part in British contests.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants, so the plural means pairs.

clue.text: Charge concerning mum and dad? Not dad!

indicators.note: not signals that the word for dad is taken away

parts.note: parental means relating to parents
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A fee relating to parents, but leave father out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing PA from PARENTAL leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental is the fee charged for hiring something.

clue.text: Such may be the trials of the medical researcher

definitions.text: Such may be the trials of the medical researcher

parts.words: Such may be the trials of the medical researcher
parts.note: trials here are tests of drugs on patients, not hardships the researcher suffers

explanation.surface: A medical researcher's troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trials' suggests hardships; it means tests on patients, the kind carried out at the bedside.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical tests on patients are described as clinical, relating to direct observation and treatment.

clue.text: Worship of the devil disguised as matins!

indicators.note: disguised means the letters of as matins are rearranged to hide them

explanation.surface: Devil worship passing itself off as morning prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the devil, and the suffix denotes a cult or practice of venerating him.

clue.text: Officer and monarch in holed vessel

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: An army officer and a king climb into a leaky boat together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holed vessel' suggests a ship with a hole in it; it is a kitchen bowl full of holes for draining.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen strainer is a bowl pierced all over so that water drains away from pasta or vegetables.

clue.text: Learner is brought into part of hospital as recruit

indicators.note: the learner and the word is are placed inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department
L is the learner driver's plate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A learner driver is admitted to a hospital ward as a new recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for the armed forces is to join as a new recruit; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Earl with doubt about queen and her attendant?

indicators.note: the word for doubt goes around the queen

parts.note: a query is a doubt or question
R, regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: An earl with uncertainty about the queen and her servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' points back to the queen in the clue, so the definition is a royal officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer of the royal household who attends the monarch.

clue.text: Ignore silly part

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of the word ignore are jumbled foolishly

explanation.surface: Disregard the foolish bit.
explanation.definitionFit: An area or district is a part of a larger country or body.

clue.text: Person arriving early in the year in a tank?

definitions.text: Person arriving early in the year in a tank?

parts.words: Person arriving early in the year in a tank?
parts.note: one born in late January or early February falls under the water-carrier sign, and a tank of water suits an aquatic creature

explanation.surface: Someone born in January who turns up inside an armoured vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tank' hints at an army vehicle; it is a fish tank, punning on aquarium, while the zodiac sign of the water carrier covers late January to mid-February.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born under the zodiac sign of the water carrier, roughly 20 January to 18 February, early in the calendar year.

clue.text: Onset of snow gets person in tent to scurry

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a camper sleeps in a tent

explanation.surface: The first snowfall makes a camper dash for cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly with light steps, a near synonym.

clue.text: Hurry to get hold of revolutionary educationist

indicators.note: the word for hurry grips the revolutionary inside it

parts.note: to tear is to rush or hurry
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rush to seize a radical educational theorist.
explanation.definitionFit: An educationist is an expert in education, and a schoolroom instructor is one kind.

clue.text: American state's principal part

definitions.meaning: the bulk or majority of something

explanation.surface: The chief portion of an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Massachusetts is shortened this way; separately, the bulk or greater portion of something is a synonym.

clue.text: New car in Italy moving with great speed

indicators.note: in puts the reworked car inside the word Italy
moving signals the combined letters of the car placed in Italy shift into a new order
new suggests the word car is remade before going in

explanation.surface: A new car in Italy travelling very fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two anagram signals: 'New' acts on the car alone and 'moving' on everything, so whatever order the car takes first, the final word is a rearrangement of all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity is eager readiness, prompt speed in doing something.

clue.text: Ring with this offer?

parts.note: ring suggests telephoning, but it is the engagement ring that goes with an offer of marriage

explanation.surface: Telephone to make a bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call; it is the engagement ring presented with an offer of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer of marriage, typically made with an engagement ring.

clue.text: Want to come in fit, but there's lack of power

indicators.note: the word for want enters the word for fit

parts.note: a bout is a fit or attack of illness
lack means want

explanation.surface: Someone wants to fit in but is powerless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A power cut leaves a whole area without electricity.

clue.text: Fat boy needs radius restricted

indicators.note: the radius is confined within the word for boy

parts.note: a lad is a boy
R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: An overweight lad needs his range of movement limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat boy' reads as a description; Fat is the definition and boy gives LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking.

clue.text: Green and red male looking fancy

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or rearranged, so the letters of red male are reworked

explanation.surface: A man dressed in green and red looks very smart.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright green colour named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Tabour beaten in modified rhythm

indicators.note: beaten suggests the letters of tabour are knocked about, fitting the drum

explanation.surface: A small drum played with a flexible rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: A tabour is a small drum, so 'beaten' looks like playing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubato in music is a flexible tempo, speeding and slowing for expression.

clue.text: Oblong piece in cloak

definitions.meaning: a rectangular tile with spots used in a game
a loose hooded cloak with a mask worn at masquerades

explanation.surface: A rectangular item inside a cape.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted rectangular gaming tile shares its name with a hooded masquerade cloak.

clue.text: Merry baron put flame to explosive

parts.note: lit means set alight
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A cheerful nobleman sets light to some explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means carefree and cheerful.

clue.text: Got fit, healed outwardly

indicators.note: the word for healed sits on the outside, around the word for fit

parts.note: cured means healed
apt means fit or suitable

explanation.surface: Someone got fit and recovered on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got fit' reads as getting into shape; Got alone is the definition, meaning seized.
explanation.definitionFit: To get hold of a criminal is to seize or catch them; both are past tenses.

clue.text: Train a group of dolphins?

definitions.meaning: the collective noun for fish and dolphins

explanation.surface: Teach a pod of dolphins tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: To school is to train or educate; a school is also the collective word for a band of fish or dolphins.

clue.text: Endless hard work? Smile!

indicators.note: endless means the word for hard work loses its last letter

parts.note: a grind is tedious hard work

explanation.surface: Unending toil? Keep smiling!
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the D from GRIND leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grin is a broad smile, here an instruction as a verb.

clue.text: Bring in characters with brains, talent

indicators.note: the letters needed are characters carried within the words brains and talent

explanation.surface: Introduce people blessed with intelligence and ability.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is hidden across braINS TALent. INSTAL is the British spelling of install.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone is to bring them into office or put them in place.

clue.text: Vicar losing head, one good man becoming criminal

indicators.note: the vicar's synonym drops its first letter

parts.note: a parson is a vicar or parish priest
I is the Roman numeral one
St, saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A vicar who has lost his head, a good man turned criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing P from PARSON leaves ARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist deliberately sets fire to property, a crime.

clue.text: Cry, having got old, weak and cowardly

parts.note: a yell is a loud cry

explanation.surface: Someone who wails because they are old, frail and timid.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for lacking courage.

clue.text: Sign of blemish that's caused part of deal to fall through?

definitions.text: Sign of blemish that's caused part of deal to fall through?

parts.words: Sign of blemish that's caused part of deal to fall through?
parts.note: deal is pine timber, and a flaw in the wood can drop out leaving a gap

explanation.surface: A flaw that made a business agreement collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' and 'fall through' suggest a failed agreement; deal is softwood timber, and a dead branch base in a plank can fall out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole in a plank where a branch base has dropped out is a flaw in the wood.
